p01.text:
## Turn search off

Set the provider to `none` to remove the browser search box and its page index:

```yaml title="docs.config.yaml"
outputs:
  html:
    search:
      provider: none
```

This removes both the reader search box and its index, so the local search command has nothing to query. Markdown twins, `/llms.txt`, and `/documents.json` do not change with the provider. Agents can still discover and fetch pages, but `shoalrun search` cannot query a missing `search-index.json`. The passage index and semantic endpoint are independent of this browser setting. Changing it does not remove those artifacts or disable a deployed endpoint.

p02.text:
## Write a custom provider

A provider is one ES module. It must export `search`, and it can export `prepare`:

```js title="search/hosted.js"
const endpoint = 'https://search.example.com/query';

// Optional. Runs when the reader first focuses the box.
export async function prepare({ language }) {
  await fetch(`${endpoint}/warm?language=${language}`);
}

export async function search(query, { language, limit, signal }) {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ q: query, language, limit: String(limit) });
  const response = await fetch(`${endpoint}?${params}`, { signal });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Search failed: ${response.status}`);
  const { hits } = await response.json();
  return hits.map(hit => ({ url: hit.path, title: hit.title, summary: hit.snippet }));
}
```

Register the module in the config:

```yaml title="docs.config.yaml"
outputs:
  html:
    search:
      provider: custom
      module: ./search/hosted.js
```

The `module` path resolves from the config file that declares it. The module is a build dependency, so a rebuild picks up changes.

### Search context

The search box passes a context object to both functions.

| Field             | Value                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`         | The page's channel, version, and language, joined by `\|`, such as `production\|current\|en`.                                                             |
| `language`        | The page's `lang` value.                                                                                                                                  |
| `indexUrl`        | The base-path-prefixed `/search-index.json` URL. The file exists only when the build writes an index.                                                     |
| `limit`           | The maximum number of results the box shows.                                                                                                              |
| `signal`          | An `AbortSignal`, passed to `search` only. It aborts when the reader types again.                                                                         |
| `readerSelection` | The active reader view as facet IDs mapped to arrays of choice IDs. An empty object means show all. Custom providers must use it to filter their results. |

Pass `signal` to `fetch` so stale requests stop. The box ignores results from an aborted search.

### Search results

`search` returns an array, or a promise of one. Each result is an object:

| Field     | Required | Value                                                                      |
| --------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`     | Yes      | A site-root path or `http(s)` URL. Add `#heading-id` to link to a section. |
| `title`   | Yes      | The page title.                                                            |
| `summary` | No       | One line of supporting text.                                               |
| `section` | No       | A section title, shown after the page title.                               |

The box drops results without a valid `url` and `title`, and it keeps the first `limit` results. It escapes all text and highlights query terms itself. If `search` throws, the box shows "Search is unavailable right now."

### Module limits

The build copies one file. It does not copy files that the module imports with relative paths. Bundle the provider into one file, or import dependencies from absolute URLs.

p03.text:
## See a variable resolve

The example project has a second snippet with two variables:

```yaml filename="example/config/snippets.yaml"
payment.request-prep:
  file: ../snippets/request-prep.mdx
  variables:
    product: { type: string, required: true }
    header: { type: string, default: Idempotency-Key }
```

Its source file contains ordinary MDX prose:

```mdx filename="example/snippets/request-prep.mdx"
For <Var name="product" /> requests, choose a unique
<Var name="header" /> and provide the amount in minor currency units.
```

The guide supplies `product` and leaves `header` at its declared default:

```mdx filename="example/content/create-payment-guide.mdx"
<Snippet id="payment.request-prep" values={{ product: "Payments" }} />
```

Readers and agents get resolved text in their respective page formats:

> For Payments requests, choose a unique Idempotency-Key and provide the amount in minor currency units.

The real snippet also includes a nested retry note. It inherits `product` from the outer snippet. See `example/snippets/request-prep.mdx` and `example/content/create-payment-guide.mdx` in the repository.

This page uses that snippet below, so the published HTML and Markdown exercise the same expansion.

> **Check the result:** Run npm test after editing. Confirm the HTML page and Markdown twin contain the same resolved snippet text.

Values can be strings, numbers, or booleans. A variable can also list allowed values with `enum`, such as `tier: { type: string, enum: [free, pro] }`; its `default` must be one of them.

Snippet defaults, project variables, page variables, and invocation values apply in that order. Set project variables in the top-level `variables` mapping of `docs.config.yaml`, and page variables in a page's `variables` frontmatter:

```yaml title="docs.config.yaml"
variables:
  product: Payments
```

Unknown names, missing required values, wrong types, and recursive includes stop the build. The document manifest lists snippet IDs used by each page.

For this slice, snippets use inline `<Var />` in prose. Code blocks are never changed by string replacement. Put headings in the page, and use absolute or `doc:` links inside snippets. These limits avoid ambiguous anchors and broken relative links until their adapters are built.

p04.text:
## HTML, Markdown, and agents

The build expands snippets and variables into the containing page before rendering HTML and Markdown. Agents read the resolved text, not a `Snippet` or `Var` instruction to execute. Components inside a snippet retain their own output behavior; for example, an interactive control can become ordinary text in Markdown. Verify the including page in both formats after changing shared content.

p05.text:
## Identify and route a page

Use the page ID for links and cards that should survive a URL change. The slug supplies the page part of the URL; publication prefixes may be added around it. Summary is short preview text; description is a separate, optional fuller account. Project output rules choose which field supplies each surface.

| Field         | Type   | Needed            | What it changes                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | string | On each page      | Stable page identity used by document links and cards; keep it when the file or URL changes. |
| `title`       | string | After inheritance | Page heading and default browser title.                                                      |
| `summary`     | string | After inheritance | Short page preview, used by cards and other configured text surfaces.                        |
| `description` | string | Optional          | Fuller description of what the page covers; kept distinct from the short summary.            |
| `type`        | string | After inheritance | Document kind, such as guide or api-reference; can select a Markdown metadata profile.       |
| `slug`        | string | On each page      | Page URL path before channel, version, and language prefixes.                                |

p06.text:
## Choose a publication and visibility

The project enables specific channel/version/language combinations. A page is built only for combinations matching its resolved values. `audiences` and `readerFilters` select reader views when the site config enables them; `access.policy` determines whether the page enters this public build. A draft page is excluded.

| Field           | Type   | Needed      | What it changes                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `channel`       | string | Public page | Publication environment, such as sandbox or production; selects an enabled publication and API source.                         |
| `version`       | string | Public page | API or documentation edition, such as v1; selects an enabled publication and API source.                                       |
| `language`      | string | Optional    | Content language; uses frontmatter defaults/enforced values, then publications.defaults.language, then en.                     |
| `locale`        | string | Optional    | Formatting conventions used in the content; can inherit a project locale for the page language and can be overridden per page. |
| `access`        | object | Public page | Controls whether the page enters a public build; this object is not exported to Markdown metadata.                             |
| `access.policy` | string | With access | Use public to publish this page; draft pages are excluded from the built site.                                                 |
| `audiences`     | array  | Optional    | Readers this page is intended for; does not control who can access it.                                                         |
| `readerFilters` | object | Optional    | Configured reader filter choices for this page. Missing facets are shared.                                                     |

Language is the content language and selects a publication. Locale describes formatting conventions in the content and does not select a publication. `frontmatter.locales` can set a project locale for each language; pages may override it.

p07.text:
## What if the host cannot negotiate?

GitHub Pages can publish Shoalrun's HTML, `.md` files, and `/llms.txt`. It serves static files and has no request handler for choosing a file from `Accept` or setting the page response headers described above. Agents can still read the `.md` URLs, but a request to the HTML URL cannot negotiate there. A programmable proxy or CDN can add that behavior. You can also publish the same built files on a host with request rules. Bare GitHub Pages cannot pass AFDocs' content-negotiation check.

`site.basePath` also prefixes assets, API contracts, `/llms.txt`, and discovery files. For a GitHub Pages project site at `/<repository>/`, set `site.basePath: /<repository>` and publish the matching subtree from the build output as the project site's root. GitHub Pages still cannot provide Markdown content negotiation at an HTML URL.

p08.text:
## Configure retrieval

`retrieval.embeddings` supplies embeddings for passage indexing, semantic queries, and hosted chat builds. Choose a provider and model when you need meaning-based retrieval.

```yaml title="docs.config.yaml"
retrieval:
  embeddings:
    provider: voyage
    model: voyage-4-large
    dimension: 1024
    queryModel: voyage-4-lite
```

To use OpenAI's embeddings, or a server that copies its API, such as Ollama, vLLM, or a LiteLLM proxy, name the `openai` provider:

```yaml title="docs.config.yaml"
retrieval:
  embeddings:
    provider: openai
    model: text-embedding-3-small
    keyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
```

| Key          | Meaning                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider`   | Required. `voyage` or `openai`.                                                                                                           |
| `model`      | Required. The embedding model ID.                                                                                                         |
| `dimension`  | The vector size. Voyage accepts 256, 512, 1024, or 2048. Other models need it unless Shoalrun knows the model's size.                     |
| `queryModel` | The model that embeds queries. It must share an embedding space with `model`, as the Voyage 4 models do. Without it, queries use `model`. |
| `baseUrl`    | `openai` only. An OpenAI-style server, such as `http://localhost:11434/v1` for Ollama.                                                    |
| `keyEnv`     | The name of the environment variable that holds the key. It defaults to `VOYAGE_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`.                             |

The config never holds a key. A key setting fails validation, and `keyEnv` fails if its value isn't a variable name. Command-line flags on `shoalrun index` override these settings. See [Passage index](https://www.shoalrun.com/chat/passage-index.md) for the files that `--embed` writes.
